hints.text: Initialize array P containing numbers [1, 2, ..., m] in order.

hints.title: Find Index and Shift
hints.text: For each query q, find the 0-indexed position of q in P, record it in the results, then move q to index 0.

hints.title: Array Slicing Simulation
hints.text: Since m is at most 1000, array slice or pop and insert directly simulates the process in O(m) per query.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def processQueries(self, queries: list[int], m: int) -> list[int]:
        p = list(range(1, m + 1))
        res = []
        for q in queries:
            idx = p.index(q)
            res.append(idx)
            p.pop(idx)
            p.insert(0, q)
        return res
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Rebuilding the entire array naively without in-place shifts adds extra memory copies.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Since Q, M <= 1000, O(Q * M) simulation runs well within the time limit.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate tracks index and moves element to front, mentioning Fenwick trees for large M.
